me:2019:q2-s2.question: The directional derivative of the function $f(x,y)=x^2+y^2$ along aline directed from (0,0) to (1,1), evaluated at the point x=1, y=1 is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given function is  $f(x, y)=x^{2}+y^{2}$

The direction vector a is given by

$\overline{\mathrm{a}}=(1,1)-(0,0)=\overline{\mathrm{i}}+\overline{\mathrm{j}}$

Let the given point be  $P=(x, y)=(1,1)$

Now, the directional directive of  f(x, y)  in the direction of vector a at point is given by

$\mathrm{D} . \mathrm{D}=(\nabla \mathrm{f}) \cdot \cdot \frac{\overline{\mathrm{a}}}{|\mathrm{a}|}$

$\Rightarrow D . D=(2 x \bar{i}+2 x \bar{j}) \cdot \frac{(\bar{i}+\bar{j})}{\sqrt{1+1}}$

$\therefore D . D=\frac{2+2}{\sqrt{2}}=2 \sqrt{2}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2019:q3-s2.question: The differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}+4y=5$ is valid in the domain $0\leq x\leq 1$ with y(0)=2.25. The solution of the differential equation is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{array}{l} \text { Given } \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}+4 \mathrm{y}=5,0 \leq \mathrm{x} \leq 1 \; \;  \ldots(1) \\ \because \frac{d y}{d x}+P(x, y)=Q(x) \\ \text { With } \mathrm{y}(0)=2.25\;\;\; \ldots(2) \\ \text { Here, I.F }=\mathrm{e}^{\int 4 \mathrm{dx}}=\mathrm{e}^{4 \mathrm{x}} \end{array}$$

The general solution of (1) is given by

$y \cdot e^{4 x}=\int(5)\left(e^{4 x}\right) d x+c$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{y} \cdot \mathrm{e}^{4 \mathrm{x}}=\frac{5}{4} \mathrm{e}^{4 \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{c}\cdots(3)$

$c=1 \cdots(4)$

or $y=\frac{5}{4}+e^{4 x}=e^{-4 x}+1.25$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2019:q9-s2.title: GATE ME 2019 | Set 2 | Question: 9
me:2019:q9-s2.question: A two-dimensional incompressible frictionless flow field is given by $\vec{u}=x\hat{i}-y\hat{j}$. If $\rho$ is the density of the fluid, the expression for pressure gradient vector at any point in the flow field is given as

primary.subtopicLabel: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics - Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, 2-D incompressible frictionless fluid flow.

$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}}=x \hat{\mathrm{i}}-y \hat{\mathrm{j}}$

Thus, velocity components in  x  and  y  directions are :

$\mathrm{u}=\mathrm{x} \text { and } \mathrm{v}=-\mathrm{y}$

Navier-Stokes equation for incompressible, frictionless fluid flow reduces to

$\rho \frac{\mathrm{DV}}{\mathrm{Dt}}=-\nabla

\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}+\overrightarrow{\rho \mathrm{g}}$

There are no components of body force in  x  and  y  direction. Hence,

$\rho \frac{\mathrm{D} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}}}{\mathrm{Dt}}=-\nabla \overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}$

where,  $\nabla \overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}$  is the pressure gradient vector

Hence,

$$\begin{aligned} \bigtriangledown \vec{P}&=\rho \left [ \left ( u\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+v\frac{\partial u}{\partial y} \right )\hat{i}+\left ( u\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} +v\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}\right ) \hat{j}\right ]\\ &=-\rho \left [ \{ x(1)+(-y)(0)\}\hat{i}+\{ x(0)+(-y)(-1)\} \hat{j}\right ]\\ &=-\rho (x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}) \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2019:q11-s2.question: One-dimensional  steady  state  heat  conduction  takes  place  through  a  solid  whose cross-sectional area varies linearly in the direction of heat transfer. Assume there is no heat generation in the solid and the thermal conductivity of the material is constant and independent of temperature. The temperature distribution in the solid is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{array}{c} \text { Area }(\mathrm{A}) \propto \mathrm{x} \\ \mathrm{A}=\mathrm{c} \mathrm{x} \end{array}$$

According to Fourier's law of heat conduction

$\mathrm{Q}=-\mathrm{k} \mathrm{A} \frac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{x}}$

Temperature distribution is logarithmic.

(or)

In hollow cylinder, area is linearly proportional to radius.

$A = 2\pi rL$

Temperature profile is logarithmic in case of hollow cylinder with no heat generation.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2019:q26-s2.title: GATE ME 2019 | Set 2 | Question: 26
me:2019:q26-s2.question: Given a vector $\vec{u}=\frac{1}{3}(-y^3\hat{i}+x^3\hat{j}+z^3\hat{k})$ and$\hat{n}$ as the unit normal vector to the surface of the hemisphere $(x^2+y^2+z^2=1; z\geq 0)$, the value of integral $\int (\bigtriangledown \times \vec{u})\cdot \hat{n} dS$ evaluated on the curved surface of the hemisphere Sis

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{array}{l} \text { Given } \bar{u}=\frac{1}{3}\left(-y^{3} \bar{i}+x^{3} \bar{j}+z^{3} \bar{k}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \nabla \times u==\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \bar{i} & \bar{j} & \bar{k} \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ \frac{-y^{3}}{3} & \frac{x^{2}}{3} & \frac{z^{3}}{3} \end{array}\right|=0 \bar{i}-0 \bar{j}+\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right) \bar{k} \end{array}$$

Let $\phi=x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}-1=0$ be the equation of surface 'S'

$$\begin{array}{l} \text { Then } \bar{n}=\frac{\nabla \phi}{|\nabla \phi|}=\frac{2 x \bar{i}+2 y \bar{j}+2 z \bar{k}}{\sqrt{(2 x)^{2}}+(2 y)^{2}+(2 z)^{2}}=x \bar{i}+y \bar{j}+z \bar{k} \\ \Rightarrow(\nabla \times \bar{u}) \cdot \bar{n}=\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)(z) \\ \text { Now, } \int((\nabla \times \bar{u}) \cdot \bar{n}) \mathrm{d} \mathrm{s}=\iint \mathrm{z}\left(\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}\right) \mathrm{ds} \ldots \ldots(1) \end{array}$$

Let R be the projection of surface 's' on xy-plane

Then (1) becomes

$$\begin{aligned} \int_{\mathrm{S}}(\nabla \times \bar{u}) d s &=\iint_{R}\left(z\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)\right) \frac{d x d y}{|\bar{n} \cdot \bar{k}|} \\ &=\iint_{R}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right) d x d y, \\ & \text { where } R \text { is } x^{2}+y^{2}=1\\ &=\iint_{\mathrm{R}} \mathrm{r}^{2} \mathrm{rd} \mathrm{d} \theta, \\ \text { where } \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{r} \cos \theta, \mathrm{y}&=\mathrm{r} \sin \theta, \mathrm{d} \mathrm{x} \mathrm{d} \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{r} \mathrm{dr} \mathrm{d} \theta \\ &=\int_{r=0}^{1} \int_{0=0}^{2 \pi} \mathrm{r}^{3} \mathrm{dr} \mathrm{d} \theta \\ &=\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}^{4}}{4}\right)_{0}^{1}(\theta)_{0}^{2 \pi}=\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)(2 \pi)\\ \therefore \int_{\mathrm{s}}((\nabla \times \overline{\mathrm{n}}) \overline{\mathrm{n}}) \mathrm{d} \mathrm{s}&=\frac{\pi}{2} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

$\therefore y_{p}=\frac{1}{\int(a)} \theta(z)=\frac{1}{2} 4=2$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{LM}}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{a}}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{b}}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{c}}=0.8-\mathrm{c}\ldots(1) \\ \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{R}}=0.4 \end{array}$$ From the figure, $$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{a}}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{c}}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{e}}(\text { similar }) \\ \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{b}}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{R}}(\text { similar }) \end{array}$$ From equation (1) $$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{a}}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{b}}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{c}}=0.8 \\ 2 \times \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{a}}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{R}}=0.8 \\ \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{a}}=\frac{0.8-0.4}{2}=0.2 \end{array}$$ From the fig -3 $$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Q}}&=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{d}}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{e}} =\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{R}}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{a}} \\ (\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{d}}&=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{R}} \text{ and } \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{e}}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{L}-\mathrm{a}}(\text { due to similarity })) \\ &=0.4+0.2\\ F_{P-Q}&=0.6 \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **0.6**.

me:2019:q47-s2.title: GATE ME 2019 | Set 2 | Question: 47
me:2019:q47-s2.question: Water flowing at the rate of 1 kg/s through a system is heated using an electric heater such that the specific enthalpy of the water increases by 2.50 kJ/kg and the specific entropy increases by 0.007 kJ/kg.K. The power input to the electric heater is 2.50 kW. There is no other work or heat interaction between the system and the surroundings. Assuming an ambient temperature of 300 K, the irreversibility rate of the system is ______kW (round off to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given:

$$\begin{aligned} (h_2-h_1)_{water} &=2.5 kJ/kg \\ (s_2-s_1)_{water}&=0.007kJ/kgK \\ [\text{Power}]_{input}&= 2.5kW\\ T_0&=300K \\ [\text{Power}]_{input}&= m(h_2-h_1)_{water}\\ 2.5&=m(2.5) \\ m&=1kg/s \\ (ds)_{water}&=m(s_2-s_1)_{water}\\ &=0.007kW/K \\ (ds)_{surrounding} &=0 \\ (ds)_{universe}&=0.007kW/K\\ \text{Irreversibility}&=300 \times 0.007=2.1kW \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **2.1** (acceptable range: [2.05, 2.15]).

me:2019:q48-s2.title: GATE ME 2019 | Set 2 | Question: 48
me:2019:q48-s2.question: An idealized centrifugal pump (blade outer radius of 50 mm) consumes 2 kW power while running at 3000 rpm. The entry of the liquid into the pump is axial and exit from the pump is radial with respect to impeller. If the losses are neglected, then the mass flow rate of the liquid through the pump is ______kg/s (round off to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.markdown:
The theoretical head (Euler's head) is given by

$$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{e}} &=\frac{\mathrm{u}_{2} \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{w} 2}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ &=\frac{\mathrm{u}_{2}^{2}}{\mathrm{g}} \text { as }\left(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{w} 2}=\mathrm{u}_{2} \text { for radial exit }\right) \end{aligned}$$

Thus,

$P_{t h}=\rho g Q H_{c}$

$=\rho g Q \times \frac{u_{2}^{2}}{g}$

$=\rho \mathrm{Q} \mathrm{u}_{2}^{2}$

$P_{t h}=\dot{m} u_{2}^{2}$

or,

$\dot{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{th}}}{\mathrm{u}_{2}^{2}}$

where, $u_{2}=\frac{\pi \mathrm{d}_{2} \mathrm{N}}{60}=\pi \times 0.1 \times \frac{3000}{60}=5 \pi \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$

Hence, $\dot{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{2 \times 10^{3}}{(5 \pi)^{2}}=8.11 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **8.1** (acceptable range: [8, 8.2]).

For air, assume specific heat ratio $\gamma =1.4$ and specific gas constant R=0.287 kJ/kg.K. If the pressure and temperature at the beginning of the compression stroke are 100 kPa and 300 K, respectively, then the specific net work output of the cycle is______ kJ/kg (round off to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.markdown: Given: $\eta_{0}=0.5$ $\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{m}}=100 \mathrm{kPa}$ $\gamma=1.4$ $\mathrm{R}=0.287 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{K}$ $\mathrm{P}_{1}=100 \mathrm{kPa}$ $\mathrm{T}_{1}=300 \mathrm{K}$ $\eta_{0}=0.5=1-\frac{1}{(\mathrm{r})^{\gamma-1}}$ $0.5=1-\frac{1}{(\mathrm{r})^{1.4-1}}$ $\mathrm{r}=5.656$ At state(1) $\mathrm{P}_{1} \mathrm{v}_{1}=\mathrm{RT}_{1}$ $100 v_{1}=0.287 \times 300$ $\mathrm{v}_{1}=0.861 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{kg}$ $\mathrm{r}=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{1}}{\mathrm{v}_{2}}$ $\mathrm{v}_{2}=0.1522 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{kg}$ $P_{m}=\frac{W_{\text {net }}}{v_{1}-v_{2}}$ $1000=\frac{\mathrm{W}_{\text {net }}}{0.861-0.1522}$ $\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{net}}=708.77 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **710** (acceptable range: [705, 715]).

me:2019:q53-s2.title: GATE ME 2019 | Set 2 | Question: 53
me:2019:q53-s2.question: A through hole is drilled in an aluminum alloy plate of 15 mm thickness with a drill bit of diameter 10 mm, at a feed of 0.25 mm/rev and a spindle speed of 1200 rpm. If the specific energy required for cutting this material is 0.7 $N\cdot m/mm^3$, the power required for drilling is______W (round off to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given data

$$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}=\text { thickness }=15 \mathrm{mm} \\ \mathrm{d}=\operatorname{dia} \text { of drill }=10 \mathrm{mm} \\ \mathrm{f}=0.25 \mathrm{mm} / \mathrm{rev} \\ \text { Speed, } \mathrm{N}=1200 \mathrm{rpm} \\ \text { Specific cutting energy }=0.7 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{mm}^{3} \\ \text { S.P.C.E. }=\frac{\text { Power }}{\mathrm{MRR}} \\ \text { Power }=\mathrm{MRR} \times \mathrm{S.P.C.E} \\ =\text { Area of drill } \times(\mathrm{Feed} / \mathrm{sec}) \times \mathrm{S.P.C.E}\\=\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{d}^{2} \times \frac{\mathrm{f}}{60} \times \mathrm{N} \times \mathrm{S.P.C.E} \\ =\frac{\pi}{4} \times 10^{2} \times \frac{0.25}{60} \times 1200 \times 0.7=274.75 \mathrm{W}  \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **275** (acceptable range: [274, 276]).

me:2019:q54-s2.title: GATE ME 2019 | Set 2 | Question: 54
me:2019:q54-s2.question: In an orthogonal machining with a single point cutting tool of rake angle $10^{\circ}$, the uncut chip thickness and the chip thickness are 0.125mm and 0.22mm,respectively. Using Merchant's first solution for the condition of minimum cutting force, the coefficient of friction at the chip-tool interface is ______ (round off to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{array}{l} \alpha=10^{\circ}, t_{l}=0.125, \quad t_{2}=0.22 \\ r=\frac{0.125}{0.22}=0.57 \\ \text { shear angle, } \phi=\tan ^{-1}\left[\frac{r \cos \alpha_{0}}{1-r \sin \alpha_{0}}\right] \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} \phi &=\tan ^{-1}\left[\frac{0.57 \cos 10}{1-0.57 \sin 10}\right] \\ \phi &=31.8 \end{aligned} \end{array}$$

From Merchant's $I^{\text {st}}$ solution

$$\begin{aligned} 2 \phi+\beta-\alpha_{0}=90 & \\ \beta=90+\alpha_{0}-2 \phi &=90+10-2 \times 31.8 \\ &=36.4^{0} \end{aligned}$$

Coefficient of friction, $\mu=\tan \beta=\tan 36.4=0.737$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.74** (acceptable range: [0.72, 0.76]).

me:2019:q55-s2.question: The annual demand of valves per year in a company is 10,000 units. The current order quantity is 400 valves per order. The holding cost is Rs. 24 per valve per year and the ordering cost is Rs. 400 per order. If the current order quantity is changed to Economic Order Quantity, then the saving in the total cost of inventory per year will be Rs.______(round off to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.markdown:
Annual demand (D) = 10000 units

Holding cost ($C_{c}$) = 24 /unit / year

Ordering cost ($C_{0}$) = 400 /order

Order quantity (Q)=400 units

$$\begin{aligned} \left.\mathrm{TC}\right|_{\mathrm{Q}=400}-\left.\mathrm{TC}\right|_{\mathrm{EOQ}}&=\left[\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{2} \times \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{C}}+\frac{\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{Q}} \times \mathrm{C}_{0}\right]\\ &-[\sqrt{2 \mathrm{DC}_{0} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{c}}}] \\ &=\left[\frac{400}{2} \times 24+\frac{10000}{400} \times 400\right] \\ &-[\sqrt{2 \times 10000 \times 400 \times 24}] \\ &=(4800+10000)-(13856) \\ &=943.60 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **943.5** (acceptable range: [941, 946]).
